h1: The 6 Best Shark Cordless Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Shark Cordless Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Shark cordless vacuums compared on listed runtime, auto-empty docks and price tier, with a clear pick for every budget.
summary: The Shark PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty is our best overall pick, pairing a 70 minute listed runtime with the lower price bucket. The PowerDetect Clean & Empty is the same runtime in a higher tier, the PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the mid-range pick, and the Shark Pet stick is the entry point.
intro: Shark model names are a maze. Two sticks can share a runtime while sitting in different price buckets, and an auto-empty dock can add a tier without adding minutes.

We ranked six Shark cordless models on listed runtime, whether the name includes a Clean & Empty system, and price tier. Only genuine Shark products qualified, and duplicate listings of one model were counted once.

products.name: Shark PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty Cordless Stick Vacuum &
products.verdict: Seventy listed minutes and an auto-empty system in the cheaper bucket.
products.description:
This PowerDetect Reveal stick lists a 70 minute runtime and includes a Clean & Empty system. Its price bucket is $100-200.

It leads because it matches the longest runtime in the group while costing a tier less than the standard PowerDetect. The tradeoff is that a lower bucket may mean fewer inclusions, so read the listing contents.

Choose it if you want the most minutes and the empty-for-you dock without paying top tier. Treat the runtime as a best case figure.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want long runtime and a self-emptying dock on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: You prefer the more established PowerDetect listing.

products.name: Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The same 70 minutes as the leader, in the $200-500 bucket.
products.description:
The PowerDetect Clean & Empty lists 70 minutes of runtime, a cordless stick format and an auto-empty system. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It lands second because the Reveal version above lists the same runtime for less. What you pay extra for is the older, better-established PowerDetect listing.

Buy it if you prefer this exact configuration. If price matters at all, the model above is the stronger deal.
products.idealFor: Owners who want the PowerDetect configuration specifically.
products.skipIf: You want the same minutes for less.

products.name: Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: Fifty listed minutes at the $100-200 price point.
products.description:
The PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus lists 50 minutes of runtime in the $100-200 bucket, as a cordless vacuum.

It trails the top two by 20 minutes and has no auto-empty system in its name. That gap is the whole reason to pick it: it is a straightforward cordless vacuum without the dock.

It suits mid-size homes and buyers who do not need self-emptying. Check what the box includes before assuming extra attachments.
pros: No dock to find space for
products.idealFor: Mid-size homes on a mid-range budget.

products.name: Shark Cordless Vacuum Cleaner - Blue - IZ363HT
products.verdict: Fifty minutes, but in the pricier $200-500 bucket.
products.description:
The IZ363HT lists a 50 minute runtime and cordless design, with a price bucket of $200-500.

It ranks below the PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus because both list 50 minutes while this one costs a tier more. Its own edge is a long-running model number with a stable listing.

Choose it only if you specifically want this model. Otherwise the cheaper 50 minute Shark gets you the same minutes.
products.idealFor: Buyers who already know and like this model.
products.skipIf: You would rather save a price tier.

products.name: Shark Clean & Empty Cordless Stick Vacuum & Auto-Empty System
products.description:
This stick lists 40 minutes of runtime and includes an auto-empty system, in the $200-500 bucket.

It places fifth because the PowerDetect models give 70 minutes with the same dock idea. This one buys the dock but not the runtime.

It works for small homes where 40 minutes is plenty and emptying the bin is the chore you hate.
products.idealFor: Small homes that value a self-emptying bin.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The simplest Shark here: 40 minutes, no dock, $100-200.
products.description:
The Shark Pet Cordless Stick lists a 40 minute runtime and a cordless design, in the $100-200 bucket.

It is the baseline of this ranking. Every pick above adds minutes, a dock or both, so this one only makes sense when budget leads.

Choose it for an apartment or a secondary vacuum. Do not expect it to cover a big home on one charge.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is the minutes a full battery lasts. It matters because a short runtime forces mid-clean recharges. Read the minutes in the title or bullets and treat them as the best case.
A Clean & Empty system empties the bin into a base for you. It matters because it cuts down on dust and trips to the trash. Look for the words Clean & Empty or Auto-Empty in the listing name.
Shark sells near-identical names in different price tiers. That matters because you can pay a tier more for the same minutes. Compare the exact model name and runtime, not just the brand line.
Floor area and number of rooms decide how long you need. A small home rarely needs 70 minutes. Match the listed runtime to the cleaning session you actually do.
Buckets run from $100-200 to $200-500 among these Sharks. The right bucket depends on whether the dock and runtime matter to you. Check the bucket on the listing before comparing features.

faq.q: Why do two Shark Pet listings exist?
faq.a: The same model appears in different bundles and price tiers. We counted it once.

faq.q: Is 70 minutes worth the extra cost?
faq.a: Only for bigger homes. For small spaces 40 to 50 minutes is usually enough.

faq.q: Do I need an auto-empty dock?
faq.a: It is a convenience, not a necessity. It saves emptying the bin by hand.
It lists no runtime figure, so it cannot be compared on paper with the others here.

faq.q: How accurate is the runtime figure?
faq.a: Treat it as a best case. Higher power modes shorten it.

faq.q: Are the Reveal models different from the plain ones?
faq.a: They carry a different name in the line-up, so check the listing for what is included.

finalTake: The Shark PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty is the best buy for most homes, offering 70 listed minutes and a dock for less than its sibling. Take the PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus for a mid-range budget and the Shark Pet if you only need a basic stick.
